svg.title: Keleven in one page
svg.text: Keleven in one page: a measured study of RAG
Question answering over the transcripts of The Office (US): three versions, each added only after the last one's failures were measured.
Learn RAG by measuring every step, not by
assembling a demo: where does a model's memory
fail, and what does each retrieval method add?

Scores are for transcript-only answers. The model's own memory scores about 7 out of 10 on the same questions.
All 92 questions: model alone vs the system
The full system was clearly better than the model alone on 44 of 92
questions, about equal on 47, clearly worse on 1.

No re-ranker, no chunk-size sweep, no embedding-model comparison.
The model alone is a small model; a bigger one would narrow the gap.

scene and detail are measured; the history is what the graph holds
“Give me the conversation before Michael says I quit.”
Finds S5E18 scene 34 and quotes the four lines before 'I quit', each
cited; all 4 quotes verified, nothing from memory.
“What is the history between Dwight and Angela?”
The graph holds their dating, married and engaged periods, each with the
transcript lines behind it. Graph-shaped questions went 5.6 to 7.6;
rehearse this one before showing it.
The detail the model gets wrong
“How much does Creed say one of Packer's cupcakes costs?”
The model alone scores 0 out of 10 (wrong); the system scores 10,
quoting the line. On exact details the average gain was +4.1.
